react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent enrichment paradigms converge on tyrosine metabolism as the dominant affected pathway. RaMP multi-DB ORA identifies KEGG:map00350 Tyrosine metabolism as the top hit (FDR 2.98×10⁻⁹, fold-enrichment 626.6) with four driver metabolites: norepinephrine, pyrocatechol (catechol), L-tyrosine, and homocysteine. Mummichog m/z-direct activity independently ranks MUMM:tyrosine_metabolism first (p=6.72×10⁻⁴, overlap 6/6) driven by L-tyrosine, tetrahydrobiopterin, and norepinephrine via the aromatic amino acid decarboxylase and dopamine-β-hydroxylase branches. MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA confirms KEGG:hsa00350 at p=0.0065. Tyrosine sits at the hub: it is hydroxylated by tyrosine hydroxylase (tetrahydrobiopterin as cofactor) to L-DOPA, decarboxylated to dopamine, then hydroxylated by dopamine β-hydroxylase (requiring ascorbate and Cu²⁺) to norepinephrine. Homogentisic acid branches off via 4-hydroxyphenylpyruvate dioxygenase in the phenylacetate degradation arm. Ornithine and homocysteine represent downstream interface with the urea cycle and transsulfuration pathway, respectively. Tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4) is the essential cofactor for all three aromatic amino acid hydroxylases, linking the tyrosine and biopterin signatures. The simultaneous perturbation of BH4, norepinephrine, tyrosine, and the catechol intermediate constitutes a coherent tyrosine metabolism dysregulation signature across three independent methodologies.
